summary: Not as a signal of direction. On 1h, price rose more after a candle whose low sat 2% under its open than after a random candle, and about as much after one whose high sat 2% over its open. Both fire in volatile hours, in a window where price rose, so this shows price moving more after volatile candles, not a pick of direction. On 4h the result rests on one SOL stretch, and in downtrends most of it faded.

verdicts.use: Going long after a 1h dip (low 2% to 5% under the open)
verdicts.text: Price rose more than after random candles at every depth on 1h. These candles are volatile and the window rose, so this is not a directional edge. In downtrends the 5% dip showed nothing.

verdicts.use: Going long after a 1h spike (high 2% to 5% over the open)
verdicts.text: This lands almost where the dip does, because both fire in volatile hours of a rising window. In downtrends it only showed at 20 candles.
Most 4h settings beat random only because of one long SOL stretch. Without it they are chance, and BTC and ETH sit inside the luck band.

verdicts.use: The same moves on daily candles
verdicts.text: The 2% and 3% settings have too few separate moves to judge. The 5% spike shows a result, but it is fragile.

notes: On 1h, a low 2% under the open gave 7,844 entries in 1,608 separate moves. Twenty candles later price was 0.75% ahead of random entries, above a luck band of -0.17% to 0.32%. The result holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. A low 5% under the open fires far less often and lands 2.32% ahead.

Read this as volatility, not direction. A high 2% over the open, the opposite move, lands 0.79% ahead, almost the same as the dip. These candles bunch up in volatile hours. The luck band's random copies keep the signals' timing but not that volatility, so in a window that rose, price moving more after them counts as beating random for longs.

The trend split shows where the 1h result comes from. Above the 200-day SMA, the 2% dip was 0.74% ahead of random. Below it, the gap fell to 0.3%, which is fragile because it shows at 20 candles only. The 5% dip in downtrends was 0.01% ahead, which is nothing. The 3% dip is the exception: 0.84% ahead in downtrends, and it held at 10, 20 and 50 candles.

On 4h, the 2% dip was 0.66% ahead of random, but one SOL stretch of 1,912 entries between Sep 1, 2020 and Sep 2, 2022 carries it. Without that stretch the result is chance. BTC at 0.44% and ETH at 0.1% sit inside their luck bands. In downtrends the 4h dip was -0.29%, inside the band.

The 4h spike of 5% over the open shows 1.78% ahead pooled, but only SOL carries it, at 1.99%. BTC was -0.13% and ETH showed nothing. Split by trend, it showed nothing in uptrends or in downtrends. On daily, the 2% dip has only 6 separate moves, too few to judge. The 5% daily spike was 4.91% ahead but fragile, carried by a SOL stretch of 337 entries between Sep 3, 2020 and Sep 26, 2022. In downtrends it was -0.99%, which is nothing.

A 2% or 3% move on 1h marks a volatile hour, not a direction. On a long DCA bot, treat it as a filter beside a trend condition, such as the pair closing above its 200-day SMA, because most of the result faded below it. Price moved further after these candles, so check whether your DCA step and take profit suit bigger swings. On 4h and daily the gap came from SOL alone, which is a reason to leave these settings out there.
